name: Vespid Dynamics Shrike Autonomous Turret SAT-2
description: A compact autonomous turret platform weighing 8 kg that can be deployed on any stable surface and left to provide automated fire support. The SAT-2 uses a combination of thermal, optical, and acoustic sensors to detect and engage targets within its programmed rules of engagement. It fires 5.56mm caseless ammunition from a 200-round internal hopper at a rate sufficient for suppressive or precision fire. The turret's AI can distinguish between armed and unarmed personnel, moving vehicles and pedestrians, and can be programmed to hold fire on targets matching specific biometric profiles. Vespid markets it as a 'force multiplier for undermanned positions.'
legality: Licensed — military and authorized perimeter defense
specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm caseless
hopper capacity: 200 rounds
rate of fire: 300 RPM suppressive, semi-auto precision
sensor suite: Thermal + optical + acoustic triangulation
engagement range: 10-150 meters
weight: 8 kg
setup time: 15 seconds
battery life: 72 hours standby, 6 hours active scanning
traverse: 270 degrees horizontal, 45 degrees vertical
story_hooks: A SAT-2 deployed in a Tier 2 commercial district opened fire on unarmed civilians — the target discrimination AI was updated with a firmware patch from an unknown source 12 hours prior.

Someone has been deploying SAT-2 turrets in the undercity with their IFF systems set to engage anyone with corporate security biometric signatures — the turrets are protecting territory that nobody has claimed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A squat, aggressive turret with a forward-mounted barrel assembly and a broad trapezoidal base. The profile suggests predatory intent—compact and lethal. Multiple sensor pods crown the upper housing, giving it a multi-eyed appearance.
physical_description.dimensions: Height: 28 cm (barrel axis), Width: 22 cm, Depth: 18 cm. Barrel length: 12 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: 8 kg of consolidated lethality—hefty enough to feel substantial, light enough for field repositioning. Dense, engineered weight.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened polymer composite housing with integrated steel mounting points and a steel barrel assembly. Internal frame is carbon-steel for structural rigidity.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with brushed steel accent panels around the barrel shroud and mounting hardpoints. Thermal damping coating gives a slightly textured, non-reflective surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with slate-black recesses around sensor clusters. Vespid accent stripe in industrial orange running along the barrel mounting rail.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not applicable—tripod-mounted platform. Mounting surfaces are cross-hatched steel for secure clamping.
distinctive_features: Triple-lens sensor array (thermal, optical, acoustic) mounted in a rotating collar above the barrel
Caseless ammunition hopper port on right side, visible through translucent polymer window showing round count
LED status indicators in faint amber/green arrayed along the barrel shroud—active scanning, ammunition status, target lock
Vespid DYNAMICS embossed plate on the left mount housing with micro-etched model designation SAT-2
Fine crosshatch heat-sinking pattern across the barrel shroud
Exposed cable conduit routing from base to sensor collar, sheathed in braided steel
Articulated barrel clamp mechanism with tension adjustment knobs
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VESPID DYNAMICS logo stamped in reflective paint on the base mounting plate. Model SAT-2 micro-etched on a brushed steel data plate. Serial number and date code laser-marked on the internal hopper housing (visible through the round-count window).
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units are well-maintained but show patrol wear: minor scuff marks on the polymer housing, light dust accumulation on sensor lenses (quickly cleaned), occasional reinforced patch welding on mounting brackets from hard deployment. Battle-scarred units exhibit scoring around the barrel from micro-abrasion and slight warping in corner panels from sustained thermal stress.
